clue.text: Management course

definitions.meaning: the running or steering of an organisation
the line or way along which something travels

explanation.definitionFit: Running a firm is giving it guidance, and a ship's heading or route is the way it is pointed.

clue.text: Judge put off over an explosive device

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to put off someone is to deter them
a mine is an explosive device buried or floated to catch an enemy

explanation.surface: A judge postpones a hearing about a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun for the person on the bench, but it is the verb meaning decide.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a question is to decide or settle it, as in judging the winner of a contest.

clue.text: A little kangaroo's thought to settle for sleep

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small musing from a kangaroo about bedding down for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in kangaROO'S Thought, with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settling on a perch for the night are said to do this; it is the verb for perching to sleep.

clue.text: Providing work keeps them busy

parts.note: reads as employers who hand out jobs, but means people kept busy by the work of providing food

explanation.definitionFit: Firms supplying food and drink for functions are kept busy providing, which is what they do for a living.

clue.text: August sitting is under one minute!

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that is under another is written below it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a model sitting for a portrait is posing

explanation.surface: Sitting for a portrait in late summer takes barely a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective meaning grand; in this down entry POSING is placed under I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means dignified and grand, and a grand building or presence is impressive in the same way.

clue.text: Approached aright in penury

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: penury is poverty, a state of need
read as a right, giving A plus R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone came close to doing the right thing while poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aright' looks like one adverb but splits into A and R (right), which go inside NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean came closer to, as a ship drawing toward the harbour.

clue.text: Getting bottle-opener after everyone else, blow up!

parts.note: the opener of the word bottle is its first letter, B
coming after everyone else means coming last

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets the bottle-opener once all the others have, and explodes in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle-opener' is not a corkscrew: it is the letter that opens the word bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosion is a blast, and to blow something up is to blast it; also an exclamation of annoyance.

clue.text: Brother Andrew's spirit

parts.note: Andy is the short form of the name Andrew

explanation.surface: A drink belonging to Andrew's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit here is strong distilled liquor, and this grape-based drink is one such.

clue.text: Rather slow and compulsive worker popular with none

parts.note: taken as written
the ant is the proverbial tireless worker
something popular is in
none is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A slow, obsessive worker who is liked by nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather slow' is a musical tempo marking, a little quicker than the walking pace it diminishes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian tempo term marks a pace a shade livelier than andante, so moderately slow.

clue.text: Somehow get in the shade

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there in some unspecified way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somehow getting into the shade on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' asks for the letters of GET IN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade of colour is a slight tint or hue.

clue.text: Couples' favourite turn in dance

parts.note: reads as a pair's best-loved move on the floor, and points to a ballroom dance named for its pair of steps danced by couples

explanation.definitionFit: This quick ballroom dance is performed by partners, built on a pattern of paired steps.

clue.text: Leave a bar and, the fellow will follow

parts.note: taken as written
to bar is to ban
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a pub, and the man will follow suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will follow' sets the fellow after the first two pieces; 'and' is a link word. A don is a university teacher or fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone in the lurch is to desert or forsake them.

clue.text: A roundabout device to corrupt other ranks

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A traffic island built in order to bribe enlisted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades, goes round and round.

clue.text: Soloist's turn to jump on the stage

definitions.text: Soloist's turn to jump on the stage

parts.words: Soloist's turn to jump on the stage
parts.note: reads as a performer's cue to leap up, and means a solo dance routine with hops and steps performed on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A performance of rhythmic footwork by one dancer is a solo turn of this kind, as in Irish dancing.

clue.text: It's natural to see point in neither alternative

indicators.note: the point is placed inside the reworked word
an alternative form of the word neither is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: It's only natural to find no point in either option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges NEITHER, and 'in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality that is inborn or intrinsic belongs to something by its nature.

clue.text: Passes a swimmer, making a gesture of goodwill

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
the hake is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone offers a fish across the table as a friendly gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's palm is the customary sign of friendship or agreement.

clue.text: Some hair — but not much!

parts.note: points to a thin strand or tuft, only a little hair

explanation.definitionFit: A stray thin strand or curl of hair is the smallest amount of it.

clue.text: Compere gets by without dislike

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
to resent something is to dislike it

explanation.surface: A host gets along without hating anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking, so the word for by wraps around the word for dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere introduces the acts in a show, the job of a host on stage or television.

clue.text: Unfortunately deaf, true, but accorded a prominent position

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly hard of hearing, yet given pride of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges DEAF and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given top billing or spotlighted is given special prominence.

clue.text: Hook-like letter.

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Captain Hook of Peter Pan is a pirate

explanation.surface: A letter that looks like a hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hook-like' reads as hooked in shape, but means like Captain Hook. The letter H is called this as a breathed sound.
explanation.definitionFit: H, a breathed sound in speech, is the classic example of a letter of this kind in phonetics.

clue.text: Egghead accompanied by retiring woman

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: and means accompanied by

explanation.surface: An intellectual goes about with a shy lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' is not a brainy person but the first letter of egg; 'retiring' turns AND into DNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as in the comic character Dame Edna.

clue.text: Men get so moved discovering something precious

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: The men were so touched to find a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like emotion but rearranges MEN GET SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel such as a ruby or diamond is a precious stone.

clue.text: Smooth-mannered outlaw dropped in the river

indicators.note: one piece is dropped inside the other

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A suave outlaw was thrown into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit but is the verb ban. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, polished person is courteous and refined in manner.

clue.text: A skilled technician is less likely to feel fatigue

definitions.meaning: a tradesman who assembles or installs machinery or gas appliances

definitions.text: is less likely to feel fatigue
definitions.meaning: more in shape, comparative of an adjective meaning healthy

explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who assembles parts has this job title, and someone in better condition tires less readily.

clue.text: Circumspection shown when taking .exercise with others around

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the rest means the others
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Being careful matters when working out alongside a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with others around' puts the word for others around the word for exercise; 'shown when taking' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Caution and self-control in behaviour; holding oneself back.

clue.text: "Blow me about in winds! ____ me in sulphur!" (Othello)

definitions.text: "Blow me about in winds! ____ me in sulphur!" (Othello)

parts.words: "Blow me about in winds! ____ me in sulphur!" (Othello)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Othello begs to be tormented after Desdemona's death

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word is from Othello, Act 5 Scene 2, where he cries to be burned in hellfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello pleads to be cooked over the flames of hell, burned in brimstone.

clue.text: A girl getting behind is put out

indicators.note: one piece comes behind the other in the answer

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is falling behind and feels upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting behind' places the girl after IS, which the clue gives as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a statement is to release or publish it.

clue.text: Rapid writer

definitions.meaning: Jonathan ..., the Anglo-Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels

explanation.definitionFit: Fast in speed, and the surname of the author of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: A check a conservationist group will find very hard

parts.note: a dam checks or holds back water
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: An audit of a conservation group reveals it to be very firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and unyielding; the word once named a legendary hard stone.

clue.text: He faces facts — retails make-up

indicators.note: the make-up of a word is how its letters are put together, so they are reassembled

explanation.surface: He faces facts, a cosmetics shop sells make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but rearranges RETAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic person who accepts things as they are is down to earth.

clue.text: The army personnel are in that position

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British army

explanation.surface: Soldiers are stationed in that place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers is a British army corps, written RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for a place yonder, at that spot.

clue.text: Memorable Communist character

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A notable communist personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable day was once marked in red on church calendars, hence a special occasion to remember.
